concept: Monkey D. Luffy is adapted around his rubber-body punches: a stretched Gum-Gum Pistol as the automatic attack, with separate development for Gear 3's enlarged impacts, Gear 2's speed and Gear 4 Python's redirected punches. The supplied passages combine story periods. Gear 3's initial shrinking drawback is not applied because the evidence says it was removed after the timeskip. Gear 4's Haki-recharge restriction is not implemented. These are Tower Defense proposals, not claims of canon verification or engine execution.

signature.name: Gum-Gum Pistol
signature.adaptation: Luffy stretches and slingshots a punch at a distant opponent. The unit uses one normal-damage punch projectile per attack, with modest hit capacity; its range represents the extended punch, not obstacle bypass.

repertoire.name: Gum-Gum Pistol
repertoire.limitation: Luffy's signature punch; the passages establish distance through stretching, not attacks through obstacles.

effects.effect: A punch is slingshotted at an opponent from a distance.
effects.reason: The base attack's reach represents Luffy stretching his arm to punch a distant target.

repertoire.name: Gear 2
repertoire.limitation: A speed and mobility enhancement. Purchases abstract its attack effects and do not model blood flow or a transformation duration.

effects.reason: Purchases permanently increase automatic attack rate as a Tower Defense adaptation of Luffy's increased speed.

effects.effect: The Gear 2 Jet Pistol is a very fast, powerful punch that propels its recipient several meters.
effects.reason: The Jet Pistol purchase increases punch damage and attack rate. The several-meter launch is omitted because no Gear 2 purchase implements knockback.

repertoire.name: Gear 3
repertoire.limitation: Luffy inflates bones and body parts to enlarge and strengthen strikes. The initial temporary shrinking drawback was removed after the timeskip; neither version's body-size change is simulated.

effects.effect: Inflated body parts become gigantic and deliver stronger impacts on a massive scale.
effects.reason: Gear 3 purchases represent a heavier hit and bounded area impact as a Tower Defense adaptation of its massive-scale attack. They do not model changing body size.

repertoire.name: Gear 4 Python
repertoire.limitation: Luffy redirects a stretching punch and, in Snakeman, accelerates it. The Definition cannot bend a projectile's trajectory or make it home; attack-rate represents reduced buildup only.

effects.effect: Python redirects stretching punches and bypasses the usual buildup between attacks; Snakeman attacks continuously accelerate.
effects.reason: The permanent attack-rate increase approximates reduced buildup. Redirection, homing and continuous trajectory acceleration are not represented.

repertoire.name: Gomu Gomu no Jet Pistol
repertoire.limitation: This Gear 2 punch has a forceful impact and launches its target; the unit does not reproduce several meters of travel.

effects.effect: The fast, powerful punch propels its recipient several meters.
effects.reason: The 0-3-0 purchase represents a faster, stronger punch. The several-meter launch is omitted.

repertoire.name: Gomu Gomu no Jet Bazooka
repertoire.limitation: Luffy charges at high speed and delivers a fast, strong double open-palm strike. The unit can represent two hits in a volley but not the separate charge or stopping pose.

effects.effect: Luffy charges at high speed and delivers a fast, strong double open-palm strike.
effects.reason: The fifth Gear 2 purchase adds a two-projectile volley and improves attack rate and damage; it does not model the charge or stopping pose.

repertoire.name: Gear 3 Gomu Gomu no Gigant Pistol
repertoire.limitation: The oversized Gear 3 punch is represented by the Gear 3 path's heavier impact and bounded splash, not by changing Luffy's body size.

effects.effect: Luffy enlarges a body part and delivers a powerful giant punch.
effects.reason: The Gear 3 path adapts the heavier hit and bounded area impact; it does not model body inflation.

repertoire.name: Gear 4 Python
repertoire.limitation: Luffy redirects a stretching punch and, in Snakeman, accelerates it. The Definition cannot bend a projectile's trajectory or make it home; attack-rate represents reduced buildup only.

effects.effect: Python redirects stretching punches and bypasses the usual buildup between attacks; Snakeman attacks continuously accelerate.
effects.reason: The permanent attack-rate increase approximates reduced buildup. Redirection, homing and continuous trajectory acceleration are not represented.

base.name: Gum-Gum Pistol
base.behavior: At 0-0-0, Luffy stretches and slingshots one normal-damage punch projectile at the player's selected target in range along a clear path. Each attack is one projectile with total hit capacity of two; it cannot hit the same enemy twice in one attack. There is no secondary targeting, splash, status or bonus damage, and no Camo detection.

path1.name: Gear 3 Impact
path1.buyFor: Choose this path when a slower, weightier punch and bounded impact on nearby enemies are more useful than the base attack's steady single-target output.
path1.weakness: Its heavy punches attack less often, and its area impact is bounded. The unit does not model Luffy's body inflation, environmental destruction or the early, post-use shrinking drawback.

milestones.tier1: 1-0-0 increases the automatic Gum-Gum Pistol's damage as a first, single-target step toward Gear 3's stronger inflated-body impact.
milestones.tier2: 2-0-0 increases damage per normal punch and deliberately reduces attack rate; the punch remains single-target.
milestones.tier3: 3-0-0 adapts Gear 3's gigantic, powerful body-part strike as a heavier, slower punch that also deals bounded splash damage to enemies around its primary target; it does not damage terrain.
milestones.tier4: 4-0-0 further increases the heavy punch's damage and bounded splash while further reducing attack rate; the primary target remains the player's selected target.
milestones.tier5: 5-0-0 adds brief, bounded knockback to enemies hit by the heavy primary punch or its splash, while increasing impact and reducing attack rate. The initial-use shrinking drawback is not applied because the supplied evidence says it was removed after the timeskip.

path1.capstoneValue: A fifth purchase adds knockback to Gear 3's heavy, area-impacting strike, giving its one placed unit bounded control as well as group damage. More fourth-purchase copies add damage and splash but do not grant that control.

crosspaths.contribution: Proposed early purchases: 0-1-0 increases the automatic punch's attack rate as the first Gear 2 speed improvement, without changing its projectile, delivery or target. 0-2-0 further increases the automatic punch's attack rate; it remains a single-projectile, single-target attack.

Proposed early purchases: 0-0-1 increases the automatic punch's range as a first stretching-punch improvement; it retains the player's target choice and clear-path requirement. 0-0-2 further increases the automatic punch's range without changing delivery or target selection.

path1.referenceExample: The Profile's scale references inform this proposal; the supplied Definition alone authorizes mechanics.

path2.name: Gear 2 Jet Pistol
path2.buyFor: Choose this path for frequent, fast punches and a self-only temporary burst that strengthens the same automatic attack.
path2.weakness: The Active Ability has downtime, and attack speed does not shorten its cooldown. The unit does not reproduce the Jet Pistol's several-meter launch or the Jet Bazooka's charge and stopping pose.

milestones.tier1: 0-1-0 increases the automatic punch's attack rate as the first Gear 2 speed improvement, without changing its projectile, delivery or target.
milestones.tier2: 0-2-0 further increases the automatic punch's attack rate; it remains a single-projectile, single-target attack.
milestones.tier3: 0-3-0 adapts Luffy's Gear 2 Jet Pistol as a faster, stronger automatic punch; it does not reproduce the several-meter launch.
milestones.tier4: 0-4-0 permanently unlocks one manually activated temporary boost of this purchased Gear 2 punch, increasing its damage and attack rate only while the boost runs; when the window ends, its normal automatic attack resumes.
milestones.tier5: 0-5-0 adapts the Gear 2 Jet Bazooka as a two-projectile double-palm volley, increasing automatic attack rate and damage as well. The same volley inherits the purchased Active Ability's boost when active; after the window, the automatic attack returns to normal.

path2.capstoneValue: The fifth purchase adds a distinct two-projectile volley representing the documented double-palm strike, while improving the existing attack and boost. Additional fourth-purchase copies do not add that volley to this unit.

crosspaths.contribution: Proposed early purchases: 1-0-0 increases the automatic Gum-Gum Pistol's damage as a first, single-target step toward Gear 3's stronger inflated-body impact. 2-0-0 increases damage per normal punch and deliberately reduces attack rate; the punch remains single-target.

Proposed early purchases: 0-0-1 increases the automatic punch's range as a first stretching-punch improvement; it retains the player's target choice and clear-path requirement. 0-0-2 further increases the automatic punch's range without changing delivery or target selection.

path3.name: Gear 4 Python Redirected Punch
path3.buyFor: Choose this path for improved punch tempo from reduced buildup, then bounded follow-up hits against distinct enemies without changing the player's primary targeting choice.
path3.weakness: The Definition cannot bend a projectile's trajectory or home it toward a target. Secondary hits are bounded and distinct; they do not hit the primary again, recurse or bypass obstacles.

milestones.tier1: 0-0-1 increases the automatic punch's range as a first stretching-punch improvement; it retains the player's target choice and clear-path requirement.
milestones.tier2: 0-0-2 further increases the automatic punch's range without changing delivery or target selection.
milestones.tier3: 0-0-3 increases the automatic punch's attack rate to adapt Python's reduced buildup between attacks; it does not bend trajectories or home.
milestones.tier4: 0-0-4 further increases punch attack rate as Python develops; the player's selected enemy remains the primary target.
milestones.tier5: 0-0-5 increases attack rate and adds a bounded follow-up from the primary punch to distinct eligible secondary enemies; the follow-up is part of that attack, cannot hit the primary again and does not represent a redirected or homing trajectory.

path3.capstoneValue: The fifth purchase adds bounded secondary-target follow-up, which the fourth purchase's attack-rate improvement does not provide. It concentrates capacity in the selected unit while preserving the player's chosen primary target.

omittedTechniques.name: Soru
omittedTechniques.reason: The evidence describes Luffy using Soru-like movement at disappearing speeds through Gear 2. The Definition has no movement or instant repositioning mechanic; attack-rate does not represent movement.

omittedTechniques.name: Gomu Gomu no Jet Stamp
omittedTechniques.reason: The passage only identifies a Gear 2 version of Stamp and supplies no description of its action or effect, so no enemy mechanic can be supported.

omittedTechniques.name: Gear 3 Hone Fusen
omittedTechniques.reason: Its central described behavior is defensive inflation that ricochets bullets off Luffy. The Definition has no unit-defense or projectile-reflection mechanic.

omittedTechniques.name: Hone Fusen
omittedTechniques.reason: Luffy inflates his body by blowing air into his bones, and the cited continuation describes its defensive ricochet effect. The Definition has no unit-defense or projectile-reflection mechanic, so neither a typed attack change nor a proposed enemy mechanic carries that central defensive behavior.

omittedTechniques.name: Python
omittedTechniques.reason: Python's central technique redirects a stretching punch instead of retracting it, allowing semi-homing attacks and bypassing buildup. The Definition cannot represent a bending trajectory or homing delivery, and no typed change or proposed mechanic carries that central redirection behavior.

omittedTechniques.name: Gomu Gomu no Rocket
omittedTechniques.reason: Its central behavior is transferring air and launching Luffy to move. The Definition has no unit movement or self-launch behavior.

omittedTechniques.name: Gomu Gomu no Gigant Axe
omittedTechniques.reason: Its damaging impact is represented within the Gear 3 path's impact adaptation, but the source-specific technique is not a purchase technique. Terrain destruction, its cited environmental effect, is not expressible.

omittedTechniques.name: Kin'niku Fusen
omittedTechniques.reason: Its central described effect is enhanced durability and bouncing back an incoming kick. The Definition has no defensive durability or attack-reflection behavior.

omittedTechniques.name: Gear 4
omittedTechniques.reason: Gear 4 is a Haki-based transformation with multiple forms. The unit does not represent the full transformation, its defensive form changes, or its Haki-depletion and recharge restriction; Gear 4 Python is adapted separately.

omittedTechniques.name: Supreme King Haki
omittedTechniques.reason: Its selective knockout of weak-willed groups cannot be represented because the Definition has no will-based enemy property or selective knockout. Its separate attack-strength aspect is not claimed as a Haki mechanic.

omittedTechniques.name: Observation Haki
omittedTechniques.reason: Sensing, future prediction, dodging and interrupting attacks are not supported targeting or combat mechanics. Camo detection would not faithfully represent those effects.

omittedTechniques.name: Armament Haki
omittedTechniques.reason: Its access to intangible Logia targets has no matching enemy property or supported damage type in the Definition. Its general offensive enhancement is not represented as a distinct Armament purchase.

omittedTechniques.name: Atama Buso
omittedTechniques.reason: The supplied passage describes hardening the forehead in preparation for a headbutt but establishes no distinct enemy effect to adapt.

omittedTechniques.name: Gear 2 Buso
omittedTechniques.reason: The cited passage describes a hardened fist that appears to ignite, but does not establish that it burns enemies. The Definition could express burn, but the source does not support applying it to enemies here.

omittedTechniques.name: Gear 5
omittedTechniques.reason: Its defining awakened freedom, environmental rubberization and manipulation of objects, living beings and lightning cannot be represented by this Definition. General strength or speed changes would not represent those central abilities.

omittedTechniques.name: Nightmare Luffy
omittedTechniques.reason: Its central behavior uses the combined strength and skills of one hundred shadows in a temporary form. The Definition cannot model borrowed shadows or that transformation; an ordinary damage increase would not represent it.

omittedTechniques.name: Afro Luffy
omittedTechniques.reason: The only cited power claim is explicitly described as possibly joking. The evidence does not establish a real technique effect to adapt.

scopeLimits: The selected evidence is bounded and does not establish Luffy's complete repertoire; this plan makes no exhaustive coverage claim.
The supplied secondary sources may combine periods and adaptations and are not independently verified canon. This proposal does not claim canon verification.
The unit uses a general normal-damage punch and does not implement Devil Fruit weaknesses, immunity to blunt attacks or electricity, swimming limitations, or Sea-Prism Stone effects.
The unit does not implement Haki access against intangible opponents, Haki emission or internal destruction, will-based knockout, prediction, dodge, interruption, or allied effects.
The unit does not implement obstacle bypass, projectile reflection, defensive durability, environment rubberization, terrain destruction, bodily transformations, or transformation durations.
Gear 3's initial shrinking drawback is not applied because the supplied passage explicitly says Luffy no longer suffers the drawbacks after the two-year timeskip.
Gear 4's Haki recharge restriction and Gear 5's awakening prerequisite are recorded as source-period limits and omissions; the upgrade paths do not reproduce those restrictions or prerequisites.
All behavior, numerical values, prices and durations require implementation and playtesting. No balance or engine execution is claimed.
